transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

If it completes a drying programme but the drum/door glass never gets even slightly warm, that is not normal and is usually a heating-circuit fault, rather than a simple drying-performance issue.

For an Indesit XWDE 96xx washer-dryer, the likely causes are:

• Failed dryer heating element
• Open thermal cut-out/thermostat on the heater
• Faulty temperature sensor (NTC)
• Heater relay or burnt connection on the control board
• Less commonly, a wiring fault or a control issue preventing the machine from entering the heat stage

Before arranging repair, the safe checks worth doing are:

1. Try a timed drying programme with the machine empty
   Run it for 10–15 minutes. Carefully feel the door glass; it should become noticeably warm.
• Still completely cold: likely heater/control fault.
• Warm but clothes remain wet: look instead at load size, spin speed, drainage, or water supply.

2. Make sure it is draining properly first
   If water is left in the drum, or it cannot reach high spin speed, drying will be very poor. Clean the pump filter if your particular model has user access to one, and check the drain hose is not kinked.

3. Use a proper spin before drying
   Put in no more than the stated drying load — your machine may wash up to 9 kg but typically dries only around 6 kg, and bulky towels/bedding need a smaller load. A poor spin can make a drying cycle seem ineffective, but it would not normally make the machine entirely cold.

4. Check the cold-water tap is fully open
   Washer-dryers use water during condenser drying. A restricted water supply can affect drying, although a completely cold drum still points more strongly to a heater fault.

5. Power reset
   Turn it off at the wall/unplug it for 10 minutes, then retry one timed dry cycle. This occasionally clears a control glitch, but is unlikely to cure a persistent no-heat fault.

Do not remove panels or test the heater unless you are competent with mains appliances; the heater and control board involve hazardous voltage. If the empty timed test remains cold, it needs an appliance engineer. Tell them: “The washer completes drying but produces no heat at all; please test dryer heater, thermal cut-outs, NTC, wiring and heater relay/module.”

The full model number should be on the sticker just inside the door opening or on the rear — likely something like XWDE 961480X. That exact suffix helps ensure the correct heater and parts are quoted.
The door glass stays stone cold the whole time it's drying. The label inside the door says XWDE 961480X W UK. No burning smell and nothing has tripped. What should I check next?

A stone-cold door throughout a dry cycle strongly suggests the dryer heater circuit is not operating. A failed heater/thermal cut-out will not necessarily trip the fuse or produce a burning smell.

For your Indesit XWDE 961480X W UK, the sensible next checks are:

1. Confirm it has a good cold-water supply
• Ensure the water tap is fully open and the inlet hose is not kinked.
• Washer-dryers use cold water during condenser drying. A water-supply issue can impair drying, though it would not usually explain a completely cold machine on its own.

2. Confirm it drains and spins normally
• Run a drain/spin programme and make sure the drum is effectively empty afterwards.
• Clean the pump filter if accessible on your machine (unplug it first; expect some water).
• If washing comes out very wet because it is not spinning properly, drying will struggle — but again, that would not explain no warmth at all.

3. Do one brief controlled test
• With the drum empty, select a timed dry setting, not an automatic cupboard-dry setting.
• Let it run around 15–20 minutes.
• The door glass and the laundry drum area should become at least warm. If still cold, stop the programme: further drying cycles will not cure it.

4. Look for an error code or flashing lights
• Note anything shown on the display, including codes such as F13 (often dryer temperature-sensor related) or F15 (often dryer heater/heater-control related). The exact code matters if one appears.

5. Optionally verify the wash heater works
• Run a 40 °C or 60 °C wash with a small load. After 20–30 minutes, the door should feel warm.
• This does not prove the dryer heater is good — washer-dryers generally have a separate drying heater system — but it helps an engineer narrow down the fault.

If it remains cold, it needs internal diagnosis. The usual repair targets are:

• dryer heating element;
• thermal cut-out(s) attached to the heater;
• dryer NTC temperature sensor;
• wiring/connectors to the heater;
• heater relay or control-board fault.

Avoid removing the top/rear panels unless you are experienced with mains appliance repair: heater terminals and the board can retain hazardous voltages, and insulation/earth connections need to be refitted correctly.

When booking repair, give them the full model and symptom: “Indesit XWDE 961480X W UK: wash functions normally, but on timed drying the drum/door stays completely cold and clothes are unchanged after two hours.” That should lead them to bring or test the dryer-heater circuit first.

Washing and spinning seem fine, and I can hear water trickling at the back while it dries. There's no error code, just the drying light on as normal. I'm not sure how to tell if the wash heater works. Is there anything else I can check myself before getting an engineer?

The water trickling at the rear is probably normal: it is the condenser-cooling water used during drying. Since it washes/spins properly, drains, has water supply, and the dryer runs with no error but remains completely cold, the remaining likely fault is internal to the drying heat circuit.

The only useful non-invasive checks left are:

### 1. Test whether the wash heater heats water
Run an empty or lightly loaded Cotton 60 °C wash.

• Let it run for roughly 25–35 minutes after it has finished filling.
• Carefully feel the door glass. It should be noticeably warm, often quite hot, on a genuine 60 °C wash.
• Don’t judge it in the first few minutes: it may still be filling/tumbling before heating starts.

If it gets warm, the normal wash heater is working. That does not rule out a fault in the drying heater/circuit, but it helps identify the problem.

### 2. Check electricity usage, if you have a suitable meter
If you have a plug-in energy monitor rated for a UK 13 A / 3 kW appliance, or a smart-meter display that shows live demand:

• During heating, a washer/dryer normally takes roughly 1.5–2.2 kW (sometimes more briefly).
• During an empty timed dry cycle, a continuous very low reading — perhaps only a few hundred watts or less — supports the diagnosis that the dryer heater is not being energised.

Do not use a lightweight extension lead or an un-rated smart plug for this appliance.

### 3. Check for obvious external water/drain issues
You have already covered most of this, but ensure:

• Cold inlet tap fully open.
• Drain hose not crushed or pushed too far down a standpipe.
• Pump filter clear, if you have not already checked it.

There is usually no separate user-cleanable lint filter on this style of Indesit washer-dryer, unlike a standalone tumble dryer.

### What not to do
Don’t remove the top/rear panels unless you are experienced with mains appliance repair. The relevant checks require a meter and access to heater terminals, thermal cut-outs, wiring and potentially the control board. Do not bypass a thermal cut-out/thermostat; it is a safety device.

### Most probable repair
Assuming an empty timed dry test stays stone cold, tell the engineer:

> “Indesit XWDE 961480X W UK: wash and spin work, water enters during drying, no fault code, but the drying cycle produces absolutely no heat.”

They will normally test the dryer heating element, its thermal cut-out(s) and NTC temperature sensor, then wiring/connectors and the heater relay/control board if those test sound.

A failed/open thermal cut-out or heater is quite plausible here and commonly causes exactly this symptom without a smell, a trip, or an error code.
